title: Fallback priority graph and staggered threshold calibrator
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: We need a deterministic, testable mechanism to decide when to trip per-dependency / per-model / per-tenant circuits and how to pick safe fallbacks. The existing heuristics are ad-hoc (static error thresholds + simple decay) and have produced either noisy trips for low-traffic tenants or slow reactions to cascading latency spikes in multi-region failover scenarios.

Goal: Build a calibration and orchestration artifact that: 1) generates a prioritized graph of fallback destinations for each (tenant, model, region) tuple (eg: same-model-quantized, smaller-model, cached-prefix, no-op/400), 2) computes staggered trip thresholds that account for traffic volume and downstream dependency criticality, and 3) provides a simulation harness to validate threshold choices against historical traffic and injected failures so we can pick thresholds that minimize SLO breaches while bounding cost.

Scope: Implement the priority graph DSL, the threshold-calibrator service (offline + realtime scoring), a simulator to run candidate configs against historical traces, and runtime integration hooks that expose the chosen thresholds to the gateway and to the Circuit Control Plane. This ticket covers design, simulator, and a canary rollout plan. Implementation of runtime enforcement is tracked in ENG-70122 (runtime wiring).
acceptance_criteria: A priority graph DSL exists and is documented (Confluence) describing nodes: model-variant, cached-prefix, regional-replicas, no-op and weighting semantics.
Calibration service produces threshold config files for (tenant, model, region) with at least three independent window levels (short/medium/long) and weighted scoring coefficients.
Simulator can replay 7 days of historical production traffic, inject failures (latency/error spikes, region outage), and produce per-config SLO breach and cost delta reports.
Calibrated thresholds rolled out to a non-critical tenant cohort (canary) with automated rollback on >1% SLO regression within 24h.
Design doc and runbook accepted by Reliability and Platform leads and links to PRs and dashboards are provided.
implementation_plan: Design spec: priority-graph DSL + threshold scoring formula (owner: Ben) — deliver draft and review with REng, PM and Design.
Data infra: extract representative request traces for past 7 days and anonymize tenant IDs (owner: Data Eng).
Simulator: implement traffic replay engine with fault injection knobs (latency multiplier, error-rate injector, full-region blackout) and metrics collection (owner: Eng).
Calibrator: offline batch job that runs candidate scoring grid, outputs recommended coefficients and thresholds, and stores configs in S3/ConfigStore.
Runtime API: expose read-only endpoint for gateway to fetch per-key configs with ETag and TTL; (runtime wiring tracked in ENG-70122).
Canary rollout: pick 3 low-risk tenants, apply thresholds for 48h, monitor SLOs and cost metrics, and run rollback script on alert.
threshold_design_notes: Trip decision is a weighted score across windows: score = w1*err_rate_short + w2*(p95_latency_medium / latency_target) + w3*increase_in_unhealthy_backends_long.
Separate floor thresholds for very-low-traffic tenants to prevent noisy trips: require minimum sample count N before considering short-window errors (default N=50 requests).
Hysteresis: require two consecutive short-window breaches or one short + one medium before tripping to avoid oscillation.
Decay/backoff: after trip, policy uses exponential backoff with jitter; automatic probe requests at 10% of normal rate to detect recovery.
Critical dependencies (eg model-store or auth service) get lower trip thresholds and automatically cascade to broader fallbacks (eg global fallback) sooner.
priority_graph_examples: Embeddings heavy model: [regional-replica (rank 0), smaller-embed-model (rank 1), queued-batch (rank 2), fail-soft-empty-vector (rank 3)]
Tenant with privacy constraints: fallback graph prunes any model variants not allowed by tenant flags; if no fallback exists, use queued-batch + notify customer.
simulation_metrics: SLO breach rate (availability and latency) per tenant and aggregated
Estimated cost delta (compute and egress) vs baseline
Frequency of trips and average trip duration per-config
False-positive trips (trips triggered but service recovered within short-window)
Recovery probe success rate and time-to-recovery distribution
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (lab): run simulator on 7-day historical traffic and produce top-3 candidate configs.
Stage 1 (shadow): apply config in shadow mode for 24h in production and compare decisions with current heuristics without enforcing.
Stage 2 (canary): enable for 3 non-critical tenants for 48h with auto-rollback on >1% SLO regression or >3x trip-rate increase.
Stage 3 (gradual): expand to 10% of tenants over 2 weeks with daily monitoring and weekly config re-calibration.
Stage 4 (global): enable by default with weekly offline re-calibration job and emergency kill-switch in Console.
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert A1: Canary SLO regression >1% for any canary tenant => immediate rollback and post-mortem.
Alert A2: Trip storm ( >50 trips/min across all tenants ) => page oncall SRE and throttle calibrator output.
Dashboard: per-tenant trip counts, fallback destination distribution, p95 latency pre/post-fallback, probe success.
